sources.title: Same-document view transitions for single-page applications
facts_used: Only one view transition may run at a time; a new one skips the running one to the end.
The page is frozen during the update callback; network fetches should happen before startViewTransition, not inside it.

The default ::view-transition-group animates position/transform, width and height; the guide calls width/height animation 'generally frowned upon' because it runs layout per frame, and says the Chrome optimisation has not been implemented.
Reduced motion is not automatic; the guide shows an explicit prefers-reduced-motion rule and cautions that 'reduced motion doesn't mean no motion'.
view-transition-class support: Chrome 125, Firefox 144, Safari 18.2 (as printed on the page).
View transition types: Chrome 125, Firefox 144, Safari 18 (as printed on the page).

sources.title: Element.animate() and Using the Web Animations API
facts_used: Element.animate() creates and plays an Animation from keyframes and timing options.
Animation objects expose finished/cancel/playState, which makes interruption and cleanup explicit.
Transform and opacity are compositor-friendly properties; layout properties are not.
sources.notes: Secondary reference page for the Web Animations API guide at /Web/API/Web_Animations_API/Using_the_Web_Animations_API.

sources.title: Understanding SC 2.3.3: Animation from Interactions (Level AAA)
facts_used: Motion animation triggered by interaction can be disabled unless essential.
Sufficient techniques include C39 (CSS prefers-reduced-motion) and SCR40 (the same query in JavaScript).
Definition: motion animation does not include changes of colour, blurring, or opacity that do not change perceived size, shape, or position.
Vestibular reactions include nausea, migraine, and distraction.
sources.license: W3C document licence; WAI material usage terms
sources.notes: The definition is decisive: an opacity-only crossfade is not 'motion animation' under this SC, while translate/scale is.

sources.title: Understanding SC 2.2.2: Pause, Stop, Hide (Level A)
facts_used: Moving/scrolling information that starts automatically, lasts more than five seconds and is parallel to other content needs pause/stop/hide.
Auto-updating content needs a control regardless of the five-second exception.
Indirect interaction (focus/hover/scroll into view) can also be 'automatic' for this SC.
A pause mechanism must not tie up focus or make the page unusable.
sources.notes: Short interaction-triggered transitions are 2.3.3 territory, not 2.2.2; long ambient loops are the reverse.

sources.title: Understanding SC 2.4.11: Focus Not Obscured (Minimum) (Level AA)
facts_used: A component receiving keyboard focus must not be entirely hidden by author-created content.
Sticky footers and sticky headers are named as typical obscuring layers.
Technique C43 uses CSS scroll-padding to un-obscure content.
Failure F110 covers a sticky footer/header completely hiding focused elements.
sources.notes: Directly constrains the proposed mobile save dock and any sticky proof bar.

sources.title: prefers-reduced-motion CSS media feature
facts_used: Detects a device setting that asks for non-essential motion to be removed, reduced, or replaced.
The reduce value can be a muted animation rather than no animation; the example tones scaling down to a dissolve.
Scaling/panning large objects are named vestibular triggers.
sources.notes: Supports treating reduce as a design mode, not just a kill switch.

sources.title: formkit/auto-animate source: src/index.ts
facts_used: Default duration 250 ms, easing ease-in-out; add() uses duration * 1.5
Disables itself when prefers-reduced-motion: reduce matches, unless disrespectUserMotionPreference is set; the option is documented as 'not recommended'
remain() animates width/height when the element's size changes
remove() re-parents the node with position:absolute, pointer-events:none, then removes it on finish
Installs MutationObserver, ResizeObserver, IntersectionObserver, a 2s setInterval poll per element, and requestIdleCallback/rAF scheduling
Sets the parent to position: relative if static
